heard: NASA used a spy satellite to check for launch damage. A shuttle launch is actually a controlled explosion. The noise vibrates your bones from three miles away. But at ignition, that sound became a physical wall. This shockwave slammed into Columbia like a massive hammer. It instantly ripped 16 heat tiles off the ship's belly. NASA feared the crew would burn up during reentry. They secretly used a top-secret spy satellite for pictures. Commander John Young actually saw the secret bird from orbit. NASA's first shuttle launch required a spy to ensure it survived.
